text:
Alex C: Quick sync — Acme Corp just signed the prelim MSA, they're asking for committed throughput numbers and a security questionnaire follow-up. Can we lock down GPU reservation sizing and fallback policy by EOD?
Priya N: Congrats! Do we have their traffic profile? peak qps, avg tokens per request?
Alex C: I asked for it. For now they said: ~1.5k requests/minute at peak, typical prompt ~300 tokens, replies ~150 tokens. They'll run a week-long POC with mixed chat+batch endpoints.
Michael R: Rough calc: 1.5k rpm = 25 rps. With 450 tokens/request => 11.25k tokens/sec. With avg model throughput ~50 tokens/sec per GPU (8-bit quantized) that's ~225 GPUs if single-threaded. But we batch and KV cache; effective tokens/sec/GPU is higher.
Eva S: We need to propose committed GPUs + autoscale burst. Enterprise prefers reserved with 20-30% headroom. Suggest reserved 150 GPUs, burst pool 80 GPUs, autoscale timeout 90s.
Alex C: How aggressive is our batching for chat? If we can get 2x effective throughput with continuous batching then 150 reserved might be OK.
Michael R: Right — with continuous batching + prefix caching we commonly see 1.8–2.5x depending on concurrency. If they use streaming and low-latency constraints, expect closer to 1.6x.
Priya N: On pricing, do we quote committed monthly + per-token overage? They asked for a blended unit cost.
Eva S: Use the enterprise commit template: base monthly fee for reserved GPUs (committed), then overage per token at hosted rates minus bulk discount. I'll attach numbers after infra confirms counts.
infra-bot: FYI — runbook created: https://console.internal/runbooks/commit-sizing-2026 (access: redwood/acme).
Alex C: Security questionnaire: they sent a 45-page vendor questionnaire with infra/networking and key management asks. Can we confirm KMS/HSM options for Private?
Michael R: Private supports customer-managed KMS via CloudKMS + HSM integrations in our private deployment. For Dedicated we have envelope encryption and rotation logs. I'll drop the exact config snippet.
Alex C: Please paste the snippet. They'll want it in the questionnaire.
Michael R: ```yaml
kms:
  provider: gcp-kms
  key_ring: projects/acme-prod/locations/global/keyRings/acme-kr
  crypto_key: cryptoKey1
  rotation: 30d
  audit: enabled
```
Priya N: Also they asked about prewarm and AZ failover. Recommend prewarm of 20% of reserved capacity across two AZs, and burst routed to region fallback if AZ degraded.
Eva S: Can ops commit to SLA targets for latency during fallback? Sales wants a sentence to include in SOW.
Michael R: We can commit to P99 latency targets per model family under normal conditions. During cross-AZ failover we guarantee throughput but will allow 2x latency SLO slack for 30 minutes during mitigation. Ops to review exact wording.
Alex C: Blocker: legal wants proof of isolation for shared nodes during Dedicated mode. Who handles the attestation?
infra-bot: Tagging @Michael R for Dedicated isolation attestation docs. See artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/dedicated/isolation-attest-v2.pdf
Michael R: I'll produce a short attestation summary for Legal by tomorrow. Also we should propose an emergency fallback: if Dedicated capacity hits 95% sustained for >5m we spill to hosted compatible model (with consent) — include opt-in clause.
Eva S: Good — add explicit opt-in to SOW and show cost delta for spillover.
Priya N: Action items: 1) Michael confirm final GPU counts + attestation doc. 2) Eva draft SOW wording + pricing delta. 3) Alex collect security Q answers. 4) Ops confirm autoscale timeouts and prewarm plan.
Alex C: Thanks — I'll update the customer. Leave any quick notes here and I'll stitch into the proposal. :thumbsup:
Priya N: One more: recommend adding a short chaos test during POC to validate failover. Quick run: 10% traffic shift to fallback every day for 3 days.
Michael R: Agreed, include a short test window in POC plan.
Eva S: I'll coordinate with Solutions Eng for the test design.
Alex C: Awesome. Closing thread for now, will reopen if we get more asks.
